title: Directing a project: purpose, objectives and context
blurb: Explain how directing a project lets the board stay accountable through key decisions while the project manager runs the project day to day.
question: Which process enables the project board to be accountable for the project's success while delegating day-to-day management, and when does it start?

teach.body: Formally: the purpose of directing a project is to enable the project board to be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager. In plain English: the board steers and decides at the important moments; the project manager does the daily running.

teach.h: When the board is called on

items.label: Request to initiate: directing a project begins
Request for the next stage (or an exception plan)
Request to close: board authorizes closure

teach.body: Directing a project starts when starting up a project sends the request to initiate and runs until the board authorizes closure. The board manages by exception: it does not manage day to day and is not involved in managing product delivery. It keeps the link with the business layer, and the process lets it make sure the project stays justified without being weighed down by hands-on management.

teach.body: Northmoor Fire and Rescue Service is replacing the data terminals in its fire engines. Executive Ruth Achebe and her board agree to direct by exception: they read monthly highlight reports and meet at stage ends. When project manager Owen Pryce asks senior user Jas Kaur for advice on the screen layout, she replies the same day. When Owen forecasts a stage cost overrun, he sends an exception report and the board decides the next step.

teach.text: Classic traps: directing a project is NOT day-to-day management, and the board is NOT involved in managing product delivery (team managers take instructions from the PM). Directing a project starts on the request to initiate, NOT when the mandate arrives. 'The business layer has a connection to the project' is a directing objective, not a starting up one.

items: Purpose: board accountable through key decisions and overall control; day-to-day management delegated to the PM.
Objectives: authority to initiate, deliver and close; direction throughout; project stays viable; business layer connected; post-project benefits plans managed.
Context: from the request to initiate until closure is authorized; manage by exception.
The board is not involved in managing product delivery.

summary: You can now explain the purpose and objectives of directing a project and its context: the board's process, running from the request to initiate until closure, managing by exception and linking the project to the business layer.

A.q: What is the purpose of the directing a project process?
options: To ensure the prerequisites for initiating the project are in place
To establish solid foundations before committing significant spend
To let the board be accountable while delegating daily management
To control the link between the project manager and team manager
A.why: Directing a project enables the board to be accountable for success through key decisions and overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the PM (14.1).

whyNot.0: Putting the prerequisites for initiation in place is the purpose of starting up a project.
whyNot.1: Solid foundations before significant spend is the purpose of initiating a project.
whyNot.3: Controlling the link between project manager and team manager is the purpose of managing product delivery.

A.q: When does the directing a project process start?
options: When the business layer issues the mandate
When the PM requests project initiation
When the board approves the PID
When the first delivery stage begins
A.why: Directing a project starts on the request to initiate from starting up a project (14.3).

whyNot.0: The mandate triggers starting up a project, which comes before directing a project.
whyNot.2: Approving the PID happens in authorize the project, well after directing a project has begun.
whyNot.3: By the first delivery stage the board has already authorized initiation and the project.

A.q: Which is an objective of directing a project?
options: The business layer has a connection to the project
Work packages are agreed with team managers
The initiation stage is planned before it starts
Products are handed over into operational use
A.why: One objective of directing a project is that the business layer has a connection to the project (14.2).

whyNot.1: Agreeing work packages with team managers is part of controlling a stage and managing product delivery.
whyNot.2: Planning the initiation stage is an objective of starting up a project.
whyNot.3: Handing products into operational use belongs to closing a project.

B.q:
Which two statements describe objectives of directing a project?
1. Alternative approaches have been evaluated and the project approach agreed.
2. There is authority to deliver the project product.
3. Team managers are clear about what is to be produced.
4. The project remains viable.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Authority to deliver the project product (2) and the project remaining viable (4) are both objectives of directing a project (14.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is an objective of starting up a project.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 belongs to starting up a project and statement 3 to managing product delivery.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is an objective of managing product delivery, not directing a project.

B.q: Which statement about the project board's role in directing a project is correct?
options: It directs team managers in managing product delivery
It manages by exception, leaving daily running to the PM
It meets daily to review each work package's progress
It takes over daily management when risks increase
B.why: The board manages by exception and delegates day-to-day management to the project manager (14.1, 14.3).

whyNot.0: The board is not involved in managing product delivery; team managers take instructions from the PM.
whyNot.2: Reviewing work package progress is the PM's job in controlling a stage, using checkpoint reports.
whyNot.3: Rising risk is handled through tolerances and escalation; the board still does not manage day to day.

B.q: Directing a project connects the project with which level that sits outside the project management team?
options: The business layer
The delivering level
The project support office
The change authority
B.why: Making sure the business layer has a connection to the project is an objective of directing a project; the business layer sits outside the project management team.

whyNot.1: The delivering level (team managers) is inside the project management team and works through the PM.
whyNot.2: Project support is part of the project, under the PM's responsibility.
whyNot.3: A change authority is a role the board may delegate to inside the project.

C.q: Which process begins when starting up a project sends its request, and who uses it?
options: Directing a project, used by the project board
Initiating a project, used by the project board
Directing a project, used by the business layer
Controlling a stage, used by the project manager
C.why: The request to initiate starts directing a project, which is the project board's process.

whyNot.1: Initiating a project starts only once the board authorizes initiation, and it is run by the PM.
whyNot.2: The process is right, but the business layer sits outside the project; the board uses directing a project.
whyNot.3: Controlling a stage begins in the first delivery stage, after initiation.

C.q: A project manager forecasts that the current stage will exceed its cost tolerance. In which process does the board respond, and how?
options: Controlling a stage, by taking corrective action itself
Directing a project, by deciding on the exception report
Managing a stage boundary, by writing the exception plan
Managing product delivery, by revising work packages
C.why: The board responds to exception reports in directing a project (give ongoing direction) and may ask for an exception plan.

whyNot.0: Corrective action within tolerance is the PM's job in controlling a stage; a forecast breach goes to the board.
whyNot.2: The PM writes an exception plan in managing a stage boundary if the board asks; the board does not write it.
whyNot.3: The board is not involved in managing product delivery.

C.q: How does directing a project help the board keep the project justified without being overburdened?
options: The board reviews every product before it is handed over
The board writes each stage plan to keep control
The board approves each work package before it starts
The board makes key decisions and delegates daily work
C.why: The board makes the key decisions and exercises overall control while delegating day-to-day management, so it stays in control without hands-on management (14.1, 14.3).

whyNot.0: Reviewing every product is quality control work, not the board's directing role.
whyNot.1: Stage plans are prepared by the PM; the board approves them.
whyNot.2: Work packages are authorized by the PM in controlling a stage.

reteach.title: Steering, not driving
reteach.question: If the board does not run the project day to day, how does it stay in charge?

blocks.body: The board holds the levers that matter: it decides whether to start initiation, whether to commit to the whole project, whether each next stage goes ahead and whether to close. Between those points it sets tolerances, reads reports and gives advice when asked. If a forecast breach of tolerance appears, the problem comes to the board.

children.label: PM handles it in controlling a stage

blocks.text: The board starts work on the request to initiate, not on the mandate, and stops after authorizing closure.

explain.body: Enable the board to be accountable for success through key decisions and overall control, while the project manager manages day to day on its behalf.

test.q: Directing a project enables the board to be accountable for success while doing what?
options: Delegating day-to-day management to the PM
Approving each work package before it starts
Writing the stage plans for each stage
Setting the work package tolerances
test.why: The board delegates day-to-day management to the project manager while keeping key decisions and overall control (14.1).

whyNot.1: Work packages are authorized by the PM in controlling a stage, not by the board.
whyNot.2: The PM prepares stage plans; the board approves them.
whyNot.3: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager; the board sets stage tolerances.

explain.body: Authority to initiate, to deliver the project product and to close; direction and control throughout; the project remains viable; the business layer is connected; and plans for realizing post-project benefits are managed and reviewed.

test.q: Which objective of directing a project looks beyond the end of the project?
options: There is authority to initiate the project
Direction is given throughout the project
The project remains viable at each decision
Plans for post-project benefits are managed
test.why: Making sure plans for realizing post-project benefits are managed and reviewed looks beyond closure (14.2).

whyNot.0: Authority to initiate concerns the start of the project.
whyNot.1: Direction throughout covers the project's life, not the period after it.
whyNot.2: Viability is checked during the project at each decision point.

explain.body: Starts on the request to initiate and ends after the board authorizes closure. The board manages by exception, is not involved in managing product delivery and keeps the business layer informed.

test.q: Which statement about the project board in directing a project is correct?
options: It manages the project day to day
It has no part in managing product delivery
It starts directing when the mandate arrives
It reports directly to team managers
test.why: The board is not involved in managing product delivery; team managers work through the project manager (14.3).

whyNot.0: Day-to-day management is delegated to the project manager.
whyNot.2: Directing a project starts on the request to initiate, after starting up a project.
whyNot.3: Team managers report to the project manager, not to or from the board.

explain.body: The business layer sets project tolerances, the board sets stage tolerances and the PM sets work package tolerances. A forecast breach goes up one level: from the PM to the board as an exception report, and from the board to the business layer for project tolerance.

test.q: Who sets the stage tolerances that the project manager works within?
options: The business layer
The team manager
The project manager
The project board
test.why: The project board sets stage tolerances; the business layer sets project tolerances.

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project-level tolerances.
whyNot.1: Team managers work within the work package tolerances set by the project manager; they do not set stage tolerances.
whyNot.2: The PM works within stage tolerances and sets work package tolerances.
